lines.trans: You fixed the ceiling lamp! The walnut wood shines like honey now!
Look right here behind the folding music desk when the lamp shines down.
Is that folded music paper stuck inside the hinge?
Let me slide it out gently with two fingers so the paper does not tear.
Handwritten notes in black ink! Can you read the title on top, Suad?

lines.trans: Why did the music stop thirty years ago—and who wrote it?!
See you soon!

words.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Collective noun for cedar wood or cedar trees.

examples.trans: This is an old cedar wood box.
The scent of cedar wood is very pleasant.

meanings.note: Elative of رقيق ('delicate, thin'); in exclamations after ما (ما أرق هاللحن! 'how gentle this melody is!') it stays invariable.

examples.trans: How gentle the sound of the piano is at night!

examples.text: هاد الورق أرق من ورق الدفتر.
examples.trans: This paper is thinner than notebook paper.

meanings.note: Primary colour adjective ('black'); feminine and non-human plural form is سودا (sooda).

examples.text: جيب لفة لزاق أسود من الدكان.
examples.trans: Pick up a roll of black tape from the shop.
The black cat is sleeping under the tree.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Jordan, Syria, Lebanon and Palestine use the old Syriac-derived month names: كانون التاني January ... أيار May ... أيلول September.

examples.trans: My birthday is in May.
In May the weather gets nice in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a finger or toe; dual إصبعين ('two fingers'), broken plural أصابع.

examples.trans: Pull the paper out gently with two fingers.

examples.text: خلي أصابعك بعيدة عن الفرن السخن.
examples.trans: Keep your fingers away from the hot oven.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمع.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Form VII intransitive/passive of مزع ('to tear, rip') in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: انتبه عشان ما تنمزع الورقة القديمة.
examples.trans: Be careful so the old sheet of paper does not tear.

examples.text: انمزع الكيس الورق من تقل الليمون.
examples.trans: The paper bag tore from the weight of the lemons.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بطاقات.

examples.trans: There is a paper tag on the suitcase.
I wrote my name on the card.

meanings.note: Means both a calendar 'date' (تاريخ البطاقة 'the date on the card') and 'history'.

examples.trans: Write today's date at the top of the page.

examples.text: هاد البيت القديم إله تاريخ حلو بعمان.
examples.trans: This old house has a lovely history in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمل.

examples.trans: Start with three short, simple sentences.
Write this sentence in the notebook.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: From ح-م-ل ('to carry, hold'); names a music stand (حامل النوتة) or lamp/book holder.

examples.text: حطينا الورقة على حامل النوتة الخشب.
examples.trans: We set the sheet on the wooden music stand.

examples.text: حامل المفاتيح معلق ورا مكتب الاستقبال.
examples.trans: The key rack hangs behind the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحبار.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخشاب.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Expressive quadriliteral verb for humming a melody softly without words.

examples.text: سعاد صارت تدندن اللحن وهي بتقرا الورقة.
examples.trans: Suad began humming the melody as she read the sheet.

examples.text: طارق بيدندن أغنية قديمة وهو بيصلح الباب.
examples.trans: Tariq hums an old song while fixing the door.

meanings.note: Paired with قلم in قلم رصاص ('pencil').

examples.trans: We write bookings in pencil.
The name is written in pencil underneath.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Pull a door, a drawer or a heavy thing; also to withdraw money from a bank.

examples.trans: Pull the door towards you, don't push it.
I took money out of the bank this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سقوف.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is high and beautiful.
I slept well under the attic ceiling.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

شوي.gloss: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)

meanings.en: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)
meanings.note: Means 'a bit / a moment' (استنوا شوي 'wait a moment'); doubled شوي شوي means 'slowly, gently'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصلح, بيصلح).

examples.trans: I fix pipes and chairs.
Yesterday you fixed the old heater.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صناديق.

examples.trans: The screwdriver is inside the toolbox.
We moved four boxes out of the hallway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضواو.

examples.trans: The yellow light beside the bed is warm.
Turn on the light in the hallway, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عالقة, plural: عالقين).

examples.text: فتحتي بابنا العالق من أول يوم!
examples.trans: You opened our sticking door on day one!
The key was stuck in the lock.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عناوين.

examples.text: خد رقم النزل وعنواننا لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number and our address, please.
The address is written clearly on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فاضية, plural: فاضيين).

examples.trans: Is room six vacant tonight?
The street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: Musical loanword (from French valse) for a triple-time piano or orchestral waltz.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد فالس هادي بغرفة القزاز.
examples.trans: Suad played a gentle waltz in the sunroom.

examples.text: عنوان الورقة القديمة هو فالس الساحة.
examples.trans: The title on the old sheet is Courtyard Waltz.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقلام.

examples.trans: I found my pen in the jacket pocket.
We write the names with a pencil.

meanings.note: Vocalized in the dictionary to distinguish Form I قَلَب ('to flip, turn a page over') from the noun قلب ('heart').

examples.text: اقلبي الصفحة وشوفي شو مكتوب وراها.
examples.trans: Turn the page over and see what is written on the back.

examples.text: قلب طارق الصندوق عشان يقرا الرقم تحت.
examples.trans: Tariq flipped the box over to read the number underneath.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بكتب, بيكتب).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: Used intransitively (تكمل قبل الجمعة 'to be finished before Friday') alongside transitive كمّل ('to complete something').

examples.text: رح تكمل الغرفة أول ما نرتب الكراسي.
examples.trans: The room will be complete as soon as we arrange the chairs.

examples.text: الفرحة ما بتكمل إلا بوجود الجيران.
examples.trans: The celebration is only complete with the neighbours there.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألحان.

examples.trans: She played old melodies on the piano.
This gentle tune is familiar to me.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لمبات.

examples.trans: I fitted a new bulb in the attic bathroom.
The white lightbulb is bright.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'why?'.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Vocalized in the dictionary to distinguish Form I intransitive لَمَع ('to shine') from Form II لمّع ('to polish').

examples.text: القزاز النظيف عم يلمع بشمس الصبح.
examples.trans: The clean glass is shining in the morning sun.

examples.text: خشب البيانو بيلمع تحت الضو الدافي.
examples.trans: The piano wood gleams under the warm light.

meanings.note: Active participle of ألّف ('to compose music, write a book'); feminine مؤلفة.

examples.text: مين المؤلف اللي كتب هاللحن الهادي؟
examples.trans: Who is the composer who wrote this gentle melody?

examples.text: اسم المؤلف مكتوب بالحبر بأول الصفحة.
examples.trans: The composer's name is written in ink at the top of the page.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic conservatory/musicians' term (from Italian misura) for one bar of music.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد أول أربع مازورات من الفالس.
examples.trans: Suad played the first four bars of the waltz.

examples.text: اللحن بيوقف بنص المازورة الرابعة والعشرين.
examples.trans: The melody stops in the middle of the twenty-fourth bar.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مطوية, plural: مطويين).

examples.trans: We found an old folded map in the box.

examples.text: في ورقة تانية مطوية ورا الإشعار.
examples.trans: There is a second folded sheet behind the notice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مفصلات.

examples.text: حطيت نقطة زيت على مفصلة الباب.
examples.trans: I put a drop of oil on the door hinge.
The brass hinges of the chest are intact.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مكتوبة, plural: مكتوبين).

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ملاحظات.

examples.trans: He wrote all the street notes in the notebook.
Thank you for that helpful observation.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: We found an old music book in the suitcase.
Gentle music is soothing in the evening.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'who?' (لمين 'whose? / for whom?').

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of نصف ('half'); used for half hours (السبعة ونص seven thirty) and quantities (نص كاسة half a glass).

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نغمات.

examples.text: سمع كل نغمة من البيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: He listened quietly to every note of the piano.
The chime of the bell is gentle, not harsh.

meanings.note: Unvocalised نفس covers nafas ('breath': خد نفس عميق take a deep breath) and nafs ('same': نفس الشي the same thing).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

نوتة.gloss: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad

meanings.en: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad
meanings.note: Used across the Levant for printed or handwritten musical notation (نوتة موسيقية).

examples.text: فتحت سعاد نوتة البيانو القديمة عالصفحة الأولى.
examples.trans: Suad opened the old piano score to page one.

examples.text: كتب المؤلف النوتة بحبر أسود واضح.
examples.trans: The composer wrote the score in clear black ink.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of وراء ('behind, past').

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.text: وقفوا كل شي، قديش الساعة هلا؟
examples.trans: Stop everything — what time is it right now?
The driver pulled the car up by the kerb.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
